cards.text: Paul is writing to the church of the Thessalonians, together with Silas and Timothy (1 Thessalonians 1:1). He's been torn away from them for a short time. In person, he says, but not in heart.

cards.question: While Paul is torn away from the Thessalonians, his desire to see them face to face grows even more intense.

cards.text: So Paul tries to get back to them, AGAIN and AGAIN. That's me calling a number that keeps ringing busy, redial, redial, REDIAL.

cards.question: Paul tried again and again to get back to the Thessalonians. Who does he say obstructed him?

cards.text: So why does Paul keep pushing so hard? He asks a question and then answers it himself, and it's all about the day the Lord Jesus comes.

cards.question: Paul asks who his hope, his joy and his crown of boasting will be in the presence of the Lord Jesus at His coming. Who does he say it is?

cards.text: Paul can't bear it any longer, so he's willing to be left on his own in Athens. Friend, I got left in a junk drawer for years, and Paul at least gets ATHENS.

cards.question: Paul is willing to be left on his own in Athens. Who does he send to the Thessalonians?

cards.text: Timothy is Paul's brother and fellow worker for God in the gospel of Christ. Before I sent out my invitations, my only fellow worker was this MUSTACHE, and friend, it argues with me on EVERY batch.

cards.question: Paul sends Timothy so the Thessalonians' faith would be ___ and encouraged.

cards.text: Paul doesn't want any of them shaken by these trials, and he writes, "For you know that we are destined for this." Then he reminds them of something he told them back when he was with them.

cards.question: When Paul was with the Thessalonians, he told them their faith would keep them from persecution.

cards.text: Paul can't take the not knowing, so he sends to find out about their faith, afraid the tempter somehow tempted them. Friend, that's me yanking the oven door open every thirty seconds to check a batch, except Paul can't even PEEK.

cards.question: Paul fears the tempter got to the Thessalonians, and that all his labor among them was in ___.

cards.text: Then, just now, Timothy is back from his visit. I bet Paul's holding his breath, the way the whole junk drawer did every time it slid open and we didn't know what was coming.

cards.question: Timothy is back from his visit to the Thessalonians. What does he bring Paul?

answers.text: Good news about their faith and love
Good news about their growing numbers
Good news about the end of their trials

cards.question: Timothy reports that the Thessalonians long to see Paul, just as Paul longs to see them.

cards.text: Paul's in his own distress and persecution, but this news about their faith reassures him. That's the made-it-home-safe text landing in the middle of the WORST day at work.

cards.question: Paul says he can go on living, as long as the Thessalonians keep standing ___ in the Lord.

cards.text: Paul is so full of joy over them, he asks how he could ever thank God enough. Friend, I've been asking that one every day since I got pulled out of that drawer, and I still don't have an answer.

cards.question: Paul prays night and day to see the Thessalonians face to face. What does he want to do when he gets there?

answers.text: Supply what is lacking in their faith

cards.text: Then Paul writes, "Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you." Next he says may the Lord make their love increase and overflow, just like his love for them does.

cards.question: Paul says may the Lord make the Thessalonians' love overflow for fellow believers only.
Paul wants the Thessalonians' love to overflow. What does he say it's all leading to?

answers.text: Blameless and holy hearts when Jesus comes
Peace with the people persecuting them

cards.text: Paul pictures the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints, and he caps it off with an Amen. Friend, the first time I read that, I yelled AMEN so loud I flung a whole tray of cookies across the bakery, and I just LEFT them there.
